packages.label: אַיִן וָאֶפֶס וַעֲנָוָה
packages.reason: These three concepts are all expressions of the same essential quality of self-nullification and non-being. 'לא' (the word 'not/no') is the linguistic form in which God reveals Himself to the humble person; 'אין ואפס' (nothingness and nullity) is the ontological reality that 'לא' points to; 'ענוה ושפלות' (humility and lowliness) is that same nothingness as a human spiritual posture. The Torah text explicitly chains all three: 'בחינת לא, שהוא בחינת אין ואפס, בחינת ענוה ושפלות'. These are not cause-and-effect — they are three faces of the same inner reality of spiritual self-erasure.

packages.label: מַלְכוּת וְיִרְאָה וְהַכְנָעָה
packages.reason: These three concepts share the essential nature of relational receptivity and self-emptying in the context of divine sovereignty. 'מלכות' (kingship) has no independent substance — it exists only through the people ('אין מלך בלא עם'), making it intrinsically a quality of receptive poverty. 'יראה' (fear/awe) is the subjective response that mirrors this same quality in the human soul — the soul holding itself as nothing before the King. 'הכנעה' (submission/humiliation) names the inner disposition that both Malkhut and Yirah share: the quality of bowing, yielding, having no self-assertion. The Torah explicitly states 'יראה בחינת מלכות הוא בחינת הכנעה', making this a single thematic family of concepts that all express the same essential mode of being — existing-for-another, not for oneself. The good/evil mirror for this package would be pride (גאוה) and self-assertion, which the Torah discusses as the force that destroys the Temple when unclothed — but גאוה itself is not equated via bechina to any nodes in this Torah.
